notes.title: Playtest the huge new Out There: Oceans of Time 1.2 Update on September 7!
notes.notes:
Since the release of [b]Out There: Oceans of Time,[/b] we have been working hard to prepare our biggest update to the game to date; a huge 1.2 featuring a complete overhaul of Expeditions and a full rebalancing of the game. 

We want the game to be the best it can be, and to achieve that, we’re bringing you into the heart of the process.

We've listened to your feedback, notes and suggestions, and have reworked the game to meet your ongoing expectations. 

You will experience a taste of these reworks during an exclusive test phase next week, taking the form of a private playtest. For those of you that own the game already, details om how to access the playtest will be shared on September 7th. 

Questions? We’ve got answers!

[b]* Who is the playtest for?[/b]
All players who already have the game in their Steam library will be able to access the 1.2 Update branch. 

[b]* What does the playtest involve?[/b]
The playtest will offer up the brand new Expedition system, in addition to a rehauled and rebalanced version of the game. 

[b]* How?[/b]
Unlike starting a fresh game, you won’t start at the beginning of the story, but further into the journey, with a pre-defined crew and cargo. 

[b]* Why?[/b]
The objective of the test is to get your feedback and feelings in order to validate and finalize the latest changes to the game before they’re rolled out. This is a unique chance for you to participate in the finalization of the game; we’re very excited to hear your thoughts, feedback and comments. 

[b]* When?[/b]
Get your diary! On September 7th the playtest branch will open its doors to all players. 

--

notes.title: Interview with Iris, Lead Designer at Mi-Clos Studio
notes.notes:
After our article on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1145290/view/3111424379008584371]Expeditions[/url] in [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i], Iris, our new Lead Designer, shares with us some insights about her previous position as a Game Designer and her implication in this project's conception.


[b]What do you do as a Game Designer?[/b]

On a technical point of view, being a Game Designer means documenting interactions between players, their machine (PC, mobile and console) and making sure when someone looks at them, they can tell they are playing a video game.

The job of a Game Designer is to create worlds, imagine how people interact with them, take into account all the technical aspects and the data related to it. This is all to make sure the data and concept is useable for the other members of the production team.

I was always driven to this career by Ursula K. Le Guin, J.R.R. Tolkien or Hayao Miyazaki, who are willing to create fantasy worlds with their own cultures and share them. Video games are a medium allowing to share such worlds, but they also have the unique ability to put the player as the main protagonist. A Game Designers’ job is to define how they interact with the world.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/e27592f626d3499aa15ab1d71fc12a97fd3acc4a.png[/img]

[b]There was huge work done on the expedition, notably to remove endurance. What were the difficulties to remove it?[/b]

I worked twice  on the production phase of the gameplay. First, as a freelancer, I created a prototype of the expedition system in 2019. It was done from a boardgame previously made by the project team. This expedition mechanic is inspired by systems found in boardgames and 4X games.

I worked again on it in 2021, on the final stage of production of the game. At that point, the team had realized the system was too rigid and did not go along with the new game dynamic present in Out There: Oceans of Time.

Removing endurance was a way to allow players to explore further and this decision was approved after several tests. We aim to create mechanics to encourage curiosity from our players, so they can discover the galaxy we have layed out for them. 

We started by deactivating the endurance system. Then we reharmonized several gameplay elements which were related to it. We kept the turn by turn way of playing to keep the essence of a boardgame. Furthermore, we wanted to keep this pace to allude to the several jumps needed between spaceships and solar systems to progress in space.

We did not have any difficulties to do all this but it was a delicate process. Each detail is important and touching one can alter everything done before. 


[b]If you were an alien in Out There: Oceans of Time, which one would you be?[/b]

I would have loved to be able to say an Osqueam, I think I am a Void Surveyor. With their iris looking at all the corners of the Out There: Oceans of time galaxy, it is me.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/1d248abf5859a62c24f19cb2d4ba2584b55fb7b0.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Discover and explore planets in Out There: Oceans of Time
notes.notes:
In [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i], you can go on expeditions to discover [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1145290/view/5216827407350277790]different biomes[/url]. This additional feature allows you to manage your crew members and hone in on their specialities. It is unlike spatial exploration where you manage resources.



Going into an expedition allows you to progress the [b]story[/b], attempt new [b]missions [/b]and level up your [b]crew members[/b].

Gather [b]additional resources[/b], necessary to [b]build new modules and technologies[/b] on your spaceship. You can also [b]trade [/b]them using the barter system in villages and inhabited planets.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/d2b05352a1ffd3526d9124a4926361a5661062ab.png[/img]

To attempt an expedition, you need to [b]scan a planet[/b] to reveal any  anomalies. repare your team composed of 4 crew members and send them out to explore the planet.

Each member possesses their own [b]class[/b], [b]health points[/b], [b]action points[/b] and [b]competences[/b]. Those statistics are created randomly when the character is generated, they will vary depending on their class, rarity and can be upgraded when the character levels up. 

Crew members all possess [b]action points[/b]. You need to manage them carefully as once you run out, you won’t be able to use the character’s [b]competences [/b]or make [b]choices [/b]during the story.   During the story you can obtain  [b]bonuses[/b] and [b]rewards[/b], which can be new crew members or unlocking a new story point. 

Once your team is ready, you can go explore! You will discover [b]new biomes[/b] and randomized [b]maps [/b]each time you attempt an expedition and you will encounter hazards: from the environment and story events. They can affect your party by giving them maluses or bonuses. Hence why the creation of your party is so important.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/19b8dbfbf737f53e583253d69d2b6f3690b86b2e.png[/img]


Will you be able to gear up your party to succeed in your expeditions?

notes.title: Manage your ship and resources in Out There: Oceans of Time
notes.notes:
In our previous posts, we showcased [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1145290/announcements/detail/5076095625049590054]several spaceships[/url] you will find in [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i].

Today, let’s see how to manage our spaceships from the inside! Let’s head to the cargo!



Your spaceship requires a [b]management of resources[/b] to help you survive in space. At the same time, you need to [b]manage your crew[/b] and make sure they are happy. Finally, it is important to aim to improve the [b]technologies [/b]inside the ship.

What are those resources and what are they used for?

First, your crew needs [b]oxygen[/b]. [b]Garden Planets[/b] are quite an easy resource to find it as they are full of it.
Secondly, to travel further, your ship will need to fuel. When running low, create some using  [b]Hydrogen [/b]or [b]Helium[/b]. You can find those elements on [b]Gaz Planets[/b] and [b]stars[/b].
Finally, as you travel, your space ship will get damaged. To continue on your voyage you will have to repair it by using [b]Iron[/b]. You will find Iron on [b]Rock Planets[/b].

You will need all those resources and more to continue your space travel. It is crucial to [b]manage [/b]them as the difficulty will increase and those resources become more valuable as the story progresses.  You will also need to pay attention to the space they take on your spaceship, as you have a [b]limited amount of slots[/b] in it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/d713ca1666b0b05e6063a0f09f74ae61499df0f0.gif[/img]


Resources aren’t the only thing you will need to keep an eye on. On the other side, you will need to satisfy the needs of your crew: their [b]morale [/b]and [b]comfort[/b]. 
It is a new feature compared to [i]Out There[/i]. 
Comfort influences your crew’s morale: the better, the merrier they will be. If morale is too low, some crew members will leave , creating unpredictable events that might affect your travel.

To[b] increase comfort[/b], you will need to construct [b]modules [/b]such as the [i]Relaxation Pod[/i], the [i]Regular Cabin[/i] or the [i]Mess Hall[/i]. This will allow your crew to gather together around a good meal with galactic views. 

To create those modules, you will need to find blueprints of them. Stock the necessary materials and construct them on specific slots of your spaceship. You can also disassemble them and repair them.




Now, you know how to manage your resources and crew! However there is one last crucial element to consider in your ship: [b]technologies[/b]. 
They work like modules however they add a [b]new functionality[/b] to the ship, such as: the ability to travel further thanks to the [i]Subspace Reactor[/i], prob Rock Planets and Garden Planets with the [i]Driller [/i]or gather resources from stars with the [i]Ultraprobe[/i]. 
They will be helpful to continue your journey through galaxies.

Some of those technologies can be upgraded when they are [b]placed next to one another[/b] creating a [b]Synergy [/b]effect. Keep in mind the specific arrangement of technologies might create new ones and make them better.[i] Interplanetary Propulsion[/i] is most effective when placed next to [i]Solar Sails[/i]. Same for [i]Shield Generator[/i] which is more resistant adjacent to [i]Void Fluctuation Projector[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/5c3c38bd1f6e769b29fd8a61e83d2b0269df8c8c.jpg[/img]


In [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i] you will find mechanics from [i]Out There[/i] with some brand new ones such as crew management and modules.

notes.title: Interview with Elian and Lilian, Gameplay Developers at Mi-Clos Studio
notes.notes:
After our post about [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1145290/announcements/detail/3111423019483165876]space exploration[/url] in [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i], let’s talk with two gameplay developers and their task in the game creation process.



[b]What does it mean to be a Gameplay Programmer? What role do you  take in the space exploration creation process?[/b]

Being a Gameplay Programmer means creating rules within the game to make sure the code in the game will go in the intended direction planned by the Game Designers. 
When tackling space exploration, we have to make sure the player can find the right planet at the right time, input randomized events, make sure travel costs a certain amount of resources… 
However, our job is generally larger than just those tasks. Since we are a small team, we are also implementing the dialogues in the game or the change of screens between each loading time… We are like a wildcard of the studio!



[b]What programs to you use?[/b]

We use Unity, as the game’s engine. We create UI there, camera angles, place elements on the map… Everything visual, really!

We also use Visual Studio to edit the code. It allows us to see the full code with specific keywords and color coded indications while we work on it. It makesit easier for us to navigate the whole game code.

Also, we work on WWise, a software used for sound. Charles, our Sound Designer, uses it  to mix sounds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/89bd13b01da9fc52f1ada2736c4a2d122bc59583.jpg[/img]

[b]What are the biggest difficulties you have encountered?[/b]

Ressource management in the ship.  All the little menus, ones to move, foraging and mining… There were a lot of little hiccups here and there. We have to think of every little thing to make sure  it matches the Game Designers vision.



[b]If you were one of the aliens of Out There: Oceans of Time, which one would you be?[/b]

I like the Laxians.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/dfa7addebf24bb13b876a32a469fd19121c9f07c.png[/img]

notes.title: Survive in space within Out There: Oceans of Time
notes.notes:
In [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i] you will get the opportunity to navigate through space to complete [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1145290/announcements/detail/3031453686300710711]Nyx’ mission[/url][/b] and [b]explore this endless horizon to survive[/b].


Spatial exploration will lead you from one place to another in hopes of [b]retrieving resources[/b]. However, all planets don’t offer the same kind of earnings. [b]Rocky planets[/b] will provide you with [b]Iron[/b], while [b]garden planets[/b] will offer [b]Oxygen[/b]. Retrieve these valuable resources by going on expeditions or finding places to forage for them. 
[b]Gas planets[/b] can't be scouted but you can probe them to collect [b]Hydrogen[/b] and [b]Helium[/b], much like what you would expect to find inside stars. But be careful when probing those! They are highly unstable and will threaten the integrity of your spaceship.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/bbe2d3efb8dd504ca492f3a92338cd997b330530.png[/img]

In your journey, you will encounter [b]civilized planets[/b]. Just like [b]villages in garden planets[/b], you can [b]trade resources[/b] with the local alien inhabitants  through a bartering system. During those exchanges, you can also find [b]technologies[/b], [b]modules[/b] and [b]skills[/b] for your crew. That’s not all, you might also end up r[b]ecruiting a new alien[/b].
On those civilized planets, you can meet [b]other ethnicities[/b]. They speak the [b]language of the Gods[/b]. You can learn various words from events in-game to better [b]communicate[/b] with aliens and obtain bonuses.


During your exploration, you may come across [b]black holes[/b]. You can only conquer them if you have the right technology. Scavenge [b]abandoned ships[/b] and  participate in [b]narrative events[/b] and discover more about Nyx and Sergeï’s grand quest within the [i]Out There[/i] universe.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/66968c0ae1791eba417e9e46fa44f6b8fe874f91.jpg[/img]

Space is dangerous and your choices have consequences. You can only count on yourself to survive!

Join the adventure on the 7th of April.

notes.title: Interview with Anna, 3D artist at Mi-Clos Studio
notes.notes:
After our article about the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1145290/view/5076095625049590053]spaceships[/url] of [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i], we asked Anna to tell us more about her work.


[b]What are the tools used to create a spaceship?[/b]

Before I start designing a spaceship, I ask myself multiple questions to target the concept art’s intention: what are the main functions of the spaceship? Shall it be big or small? Is the design aerodynamic or intimidating? I ask myself all those questions to not be out of scope. I develop the concept art with a moodboard to keep in mind a certain palette of colors, or to pin out details that could be interesting for the spaceship.

For modeling, I like to use Blender which offers new tools to ease my work. I start with the silhouettes of the main part of the ship. I make them dynamic and linked back to the concept art, it also helps me to differentiate them from other parts of the spaceship. If we are satisfied by this first step, I can start modeling details without going too in-depth.

Once modeling is done and the UV applied, I import the model in Substance Painter to do the textures. I love this step as it allows me to play around with the colors, create patterns in harmony with the shape of the ship and create lights to give an ambiance. What I love above everything else is to create a story with the textures I come up with. For example, are those old engines clogged by time? Is the ship bodywork starting to rust? We can draw a lot of things to give life to our items. Finally, I import the spaceship in Unity to test it and see it fly by itself!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/ea7f5fb3910a3a605c77b06678f0e03b7265a703.png[/img]

[b]Among all the spaceships, which was the one you preferred to create?[/b]

I really enjoyed doing the Archon’s spaceship. When the team submitted the idea, I couldn’t see myself creating such a detailed ship. I took it as a challenge to see what I was able to do. I asked for some advice from my coworkers to get some tricks to model it and see if my workflow was efficient. I am also lucky to have a spouse with ideas to make modelling more efficient. Furthermore, let’s be real, this ship is so cool, isn’t it?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/954dc6da90fe0834ed5092c5a037d321eaf58795.jpg[/img]

[b]What do you enjoy the most in your work?[/b]

I love modeling and texturing, but what I love above everything else is to be able to contribute to the creation of the game with my own tastes. See the game being developed by an efficient and lovely team.


[b]If you were one of the aliens of Out There: Oceans of Time, which one would you be?[/b]

I think I would be a Juge Architect. It is a gigantic bird, which is neat, and it is unable to dance right, just like me.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/bcec9a9a308fd9b5a195f4c25526aa9e002694de.gif[/img]

notes.title: Interview with Coralie, 3D artist at Mi-Clos Studio
notes.notes:
Following our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1145290/view/3026954876756763028]article on the Archon[/url], we asked Coralie to tell us more about her work.



[b]What tools did you use when you drafted this character?[/b]

I started to sculpt a high poly piece on Zbrush, which is a model at high resolution. I imported it in Blender to grid it at a lower resolution, it is more optimized for video games.

Then, still on Blender, I unfolded the Uvs. It's a 3D process to project a 2D picture on a 3D model to apply texture. I put the low resolution on Substance Painter to apply and paint the textures. 

Finally, I imported everything on Unity to finalize the character creation in the game. It is with this final step that we can check if everything worked together and if they are still some details to be refined. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/e6ca578d8201219a3c297c6b574b5856549a0af0.png[/img]


[b]What are the difficulties you encountered?[/b]

The conception of the Archon took me a lot of time. He is one of the characters that took me the most work compared to Nyx and Sergei for example.

The Archon is made of a lot of irregular details and lots of spikes and tiny “parts” that go over the model. He was really hard to sculpt and it was even harder when I had to grid it on low resolution, because it is made of lots of little details that I had to do one by one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/d5e5bf2e0c85875558d18430652a43cb54c01e23.png[/img]

notes.title: Discover the Archon, the main antagonist of Out There: Oceans of Time
notes.notes:
After meeting [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1145290/view/3031453686300710710]the main characters[/url] of [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i] and visiting some of this [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1145290/view/5216827407350277790]universe's planets[/url], we would like to introduce a very important character: the Archon.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/9ee507d582dea9cbee0139eb91aa2a8aeed68cf5.png[/img]


The main antagonist of the game, he is part of the Lord species :  chameleon-like creatures able to drain and exploit the strength and powers of people around them. Submissive to the laws of the Gods Cube, there are few Lords in the galaxy and most of them live on the planet of Russian Ark.

If Lords are one of the most powerful and intelligent species, the Archon is their strongest member! 
He is a genetic anomaly and he isn’t subject to the Gods Cube’s influence and can use his powers as he pleases.
What would you do if you could escape from your destiny?


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/ccfaa02c6075991a1059fb6e472858c67a103edf.jpg[/img]


The Archon decided to use his powers for himself and lead a rebellion in the galaxy. 
In consequence, the Lords, helped by [i]Organizatsiya[/i], allied themselves to track down the Archon
and to send him to the Mausoleum of Eternity, an isolated prison planet.

To secure the convoy, the [i]Organizatsiya[/i] entrust the Archon to Captain Nyx and his crew, and appoint Lieutenant Scientist Sergei to accompany them. 

But obviously the mission will not go as planned.
The failure of their mission endangers the whole galaxy, very quickly guilt will come and make them doubt the relevance of their choices.
Are they really able to make up for their mistake?
Fortunately they will not be alone and can count on the help of their overpowered crew and strange entities.
Their quest for redemption will then lead them to the far reaches of space, where nobody ever comes back ...



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/6883be77499e40d04406f03ac5c2979eb8f40a41.jpg[/img]


The concept art for the Archon was very important. Indeed, in one glance, the player needs to understand what he is facing, its aspects and story. We wanted to showcase its power, independence while keeping in mind he is an evil and dangerous character.

Lords have an appearance of giant wolves, we created the Archon on this base. Lords have light fur and blue eyes, in contrast, the Archon has dark fur and red eyes. For the fur of both Lords and Archon, we were inspired by statues made out of tyres made by artists like Yong Ho Ji and Blake McFarland.   


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/129100e375e84cc25faa4d3f28f67967bab099db.png[/img]

notes.title: Interview with Sarah, 3D artist at Mi-Clos Studio
notes.notes:
Following [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1145290/view/5216827407350277790]our article on biomes[/url], we asked Sarah to tell us more about her work.


[b]What tools have you used to create those biomes?[/b]

There are several steps to create a biome in OT2. The first step is the blocking that allows you to quickly create a shape to the future assets that will be put on the expedition map. Depending on the used squares, we need to find elements that will complement both the concept and the game design (spikes for squares with the “bloody” damage effects, mountains for blocked squares etc) and interest points as well (temples, villages etc).

Depending on the type of item created, I use Blender and ZBrush to sculpt more organics forms or details. At the same time, I create 3 different types of textures for the ground, each one will have different difficulty levels to be walked on. I also use Substance Painter and Substance Designer for the textures. However, I have a hard time quitting my old habits and I go back on Handpaint and sometimes use Photoshop instead!

One of the last steps is to import in the software models and textures, and import all the elements of the map that will be found on the squares of the expedition map. Finally, I define the light of the environment and the colors of it through post-processing in the aim of giving each biome a unique identity. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/50241fedfe9d48d030f2778cb95b9ccef2996d27.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/e54283a7f6a19cdc70699250f38922b308a41039.png[/img]


[b]How did you find your inspiration?[/b]

Before starting a new biome, generally, I receive the illustrations of Benjamin Carré, our concept artist, as a reference. He is the first one to present colors, ambiance and shapes for the environment. From this, I will decline the same illustration multiple times depending on my needs (for variety’s sake or to maintain the game design intentions).

What I enjoy in a project such as OT2 is the diversity of planets in game, which allows you to have a lot of liberty when you create each environment. When there are no concepts for a planet, I use references linked to the art style and the ambiance of the biome (especially for points of interests or even whole biomes). It is an exercise that I enjoy as it is very motivating and enriching to imagine new things in a vast universe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/93fe9e3d60616de25754970796e55a4136a81ea5.jpg[/img]


[b]Which biome did you prefer creating and why?[/b]

If I had to pick one, I would pick one of the garden planets composed of waterfalls, lotus and a dense and lush vegetation. It holds a special place in my heart because I learned a lot while creating it, especially on shaders, I collaborated with Antoine, a technical artist coworker. The plant diversity, the colors, the verticality of the giant bamboos and the ever-present water in this biome give it a tropical and troubling atmosphere. I had a lot of fun creating it and I hope players will enjoy exploring it!




[b]If you were a species of Out There: Oceans of Time, which one would you be?[/b]

Difficult question! I don’t know which alien I would be but I enjoy the story of the Zeros. They can only dream once in their life and that marks the accomplishment of something to them. Some Zeros wait for this dream eagerly and sleep awaiting for it to arrive. They sleep hoping for something that might never happen. I can’t explain it but I find this quest of an ephemeral vision very poetic and touching.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/88d2b0c1794342667a4441e78ab1ee48cbf015f0.png[/img]

notes.title: Let’s discover some biomes of Out There: Oceans of Time
notes.notes:
Last month, we offered some insights on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1145290/view/3031453686300710710]Nyx and Sergei[/url]. 
This month, what about an expedition to discover some biomes? 
Buckle up as we travel to the first planet!



In [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i], you traverse the vastness of space and find multiple planets on your way. You can probe and drill on them to retrieve essential resources to continue your journey. However, on some of them, you have the opportunity to explore the surface in an expedition. It will allow you to find other kinds of resources, such as plants and minerals, and unlock new technologies.

Each expedition is generated like a maze.
Maps will possess 3 types of squares: impassable squares, obstacle squares and finally squares with special effects. The expedition’s objective is from a certain number of squares away from your landing square. Each movement from a square to another will cost you some action points. So, you need to find the most effective way to reach the objective square within the amount of action points you possess, otherwise, each step will cost you life points!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/e6b67bb5d5ded9b69d501f533f6c72e443a07a0b.png[/img]


To better your immersion into this universe, planets possess different biomes. Each one has different specificities. Let’s discover them!

There are two main types of planets to discover: rocky planets and garden planets.

For the rocky planets, the difficulty was to make the environment soft and beautiful while maintaining this “rock” appearance and essence. For that, it was important to get away from the cliché shades of grey and dull like images of rocks.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/51dd4e47919035cab10ea5eb7736b47b9ed38c91.gif[/img]
In this first biome, we decided to go for a grey palette and use another form of rocks: clay. Landforms are like furnaces. Fumaroles and red cinders give colors and nuances to this cold landscape.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/0de6e432030968748fa023a42f6e99d378c2dbf9.gif[/img]
In this second rocky biome, we kept the brute aspect of rocks, shaped like spikes. Darker than the previous ones, this time white cinders create the needed contrast. Red grass gives the final touch to illuminate this dark biome.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/58b50721d31dd8dae5a51fa115719e7bfa011433.gif[/img]
In this last rocky biome, everything is different. In an ochre palette, this biome is luminous and warm. Colors such as brown and orange were used in this one. The landscape is flat and way less frightening even if there are some spikes here and there. 


It is now time to look at the garden biomes!



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/ed834a7f8fc75de85ad16d8953fd5ea04034b08b.gif[/img]
No those aren’t pancakes filled with maple syrup sauce on top, those are mushrooms! In this biome, vegetation is imposing and luminous to contrast from the rocky biomes.The yellow and brown colors give a warm atmosphere completed by wheat fields. 
This biome also possesses rocks but it isn’t the most present element and its very light color makes blends in the landscape.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/f142aa88e41e8a54fecb2c46202f8c547a28bb1b.gif[/img]
For this last biome, let’s discover lush vegetation, an almost oppressing one. Made of gigantic bamboos and huge leafs, this biome is a jungle reminding us we are travellers on a different planet, so far away from our solar system.
The ground and rocks are covered with fresh green moss. Humidity is present with all the water sources dispatched in the middle of this jungle, making it look like a giant swamp. Warm colors were added through red flowers or yellow leafs to give an impression of infinity to this garden planet.



That’s where our journey ends.

We hope you enjoyed the view and feel ready for more explorations!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1145290/Out_There_Oceans_of_Time/

notes.title: Interview with Mado, Narrative Designer at Mi-Clos Studio
notes.notes:
[b]What do you enjoy the most about your job?[/b]

As a narrative designer, it is the power to give life to a story; creating a universe through the use of game design tools. I want to create interactive emotions and continuously imagine how players will make the game’s thematics their own. That is the main reason I love my job. It is an exchange between what we want to tell and how players will interact with those stories and experiences. We won’t ever be able to control everything but when the “magic” works, when players feel concerned by the characters struggles, that’s when we can be glad with the unique experience we have created.



[b]What do you enjoy the most in the [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i] universe?[/b]

The whole [i]Out There[/i] franchise offers a gigantic universe that has issues close to our own problems. Fibre Tigre has been able to give life to current scientifics questions. It is fascinating to be able to immerse yourself in those gears and try to create strong emotions out of it. On one side, you have all the complexity of science-fiction that seems unreachable, on the other side you will play as relatable people that have to pilot a spaceship, facing dilemmas and choices.



[b]What are the tools you are using?[/b]

To successfully achieve this link between a complete storytelling game and the game design needs, I use gigantic excel tabs listing all technical requirements. After understanding the game’s framework, mechanics and specificity, I can start the creation of a storybeat: a technical cut of the story within the game. 
To write the dialogues, I got in the habit of working alongside Celtx. However, there are numerous technical constraints pushing us outside of the usual script. The story is huge, narration is complex and the gameplay is centered around the mechanism of management and survival. Which means, each dialogue, each decision, each interaction has to be introduced in a logical way within the global game design of the game. ([i]What should be the background picture? Which resource is necessary to unlock this dialogue? Where should each character be while talking to each other?...[/i])



[b]If you could be an alien race from Out There: Oceans of Time, which one would you be?[/b]

Honestly, I would be a [i]Forager[/i], an alien race able to communicate through smells. With my essential oil diffuser on my desk and my room odorizer, I feel close to them. Furthermore, it is an important race in [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i]! Do not underestimate them!

notes.title: Discover Nyx and Sergei, the main characters of Out There: Oceans of Time.
notes.notes:
While waiting for [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i] release this year, would you be interested in learning more about the game, its conception or the story of its characters?
Today, let’s go on an adventure through this first article, about our two main characters: Nyx and Sergei. 

Maybe you already know Nyx?
You know, this woman that appears in the game’s illustrations and trailer, and in Out There: Chronicles as well.
However, do you really know her? What do you know about this woman promoted from secondary character to main character in our new game?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/7912f5db5e4622bb84283b976ecb671c959a229e.png[/img]

Natural leader, Captain Nyx comes from the American colony: [i]America[/i]. Thanks to her strong personality and her confidence in the face of conflicts, she was able to get away from her superiors grasp. She now lives the life of an adventurer in her spaceship the [i]Vanguard[/i].

Because of her aptitudes, she is contacted by the [i]Organizatsiya[/i], the Russian colony. Indeed, the colony was able to seize the Archon, a dangerous and powerful entity. 
The [i]Organizatsiya [/i]requires Captain Nyx’ help to bring the prisoner to the [i]Mausoleum of Eternity[/i], its final destination.

To help her in this endeavor, the Russian colony sends out the scientist officer: Sergei. The man is very different from Nyx. He is shorter and less athletic. Fearful, he lets his emotions get the best of him. Sergei was chosen as the most brilliant scientist of the colony. He is able to solve any problems on a spaceship. He is also a xenolinguiste, he can talk almost all languages in the galaxy. Younger and less experienced than Nyx, he is thriving to learn and is happy to travel in her company. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/7e44311f7e754ebd7c447a42e5d310a5f0b8b9ae.png[/img]

Those two characters create an unconventional duo.
From a cordial agreement and professional relationship, our heroes’ relationship will evolve in a strong one, linked to the destiny of the whole universe.
Naturally, their mission won’t end up as they expected.

The Archon is able to break free from their spaceship, bringing disorder and chaos in its way.

Our two heroes will have to find the Archon and arrest it, once again. They won’t be able to succeed alone and will search for help in their quest. But like every human, they will have to face their own wrong decisions based on their judgement…

It is where your adventure starts, help Nyx and Sergei to achieve their mission.

notes.title: Codex: The Zeros
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/f07f1ad6a53f32a129470ccbff1c9c7c7a8d33d0.jpg[/img]

Welcome to the first Codex entry, where we will share regular information about the Out There universe. Today, we will focus on Zeros - one of the many alien species inhabiting the galaxy. 

Zeros love the Gods. These insects are the most savage - and mysterious - warriors in the known universe. Fierce and powerful, no other species has ever defeated them - with the exception of one extraordinary woman named Nyx. Zeros know no lies, property or fatigue and have thus been enslaved for profit by cunning races like humans.

The location of their mother planet, Origin, is shrouded in secrecy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/418068c2dbab95dffa2d9722fb80d3f614dee6ab.jpg[/img]

In the past, Zeros could dream. Today, they have lost this capacity and the species is vegatitive and unable to adapt to the progress of the universe. Once in their lives, they may be able to dream again. This sacred vision is fleeting and delicate, symbolising a state of enlightenment. Once a Zero has dreamt, it must paint the motif of their dream onto a white mask. Wearing this white mask gives the right to appeal to Power, a sacred telekinetic force capable of everything. Some Zeros never dream and those who do hope in vain for a new dream. As such, when you meet a Zero, you will likely find it asleep. However, it isn’t sleeping: it is searching.

notes.title: Modern Wolf's Meet the Devs: Mi-Clos Studio
notes.notes:
[url=https://modernwolf.net/]We are Modern Wolf[/url], a progressive publisher based in the UK that will be publishing Out There: Oceans of Time, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/publisher/ModernWolf]as well as a plethora of other games[/url], in 2020. We've recently focused on our developers in a series of Meet the Devs interviews that have been going out across our [url=https://twitter.com/ModernWolfLtd]social channels[/url] in recent weeks. 

Most recently, Mi-Clos Studio allowed MoNext up to the plate in Modern Wolf's Meet the Devs Series is Mi Clos Studio. The studio have already given the world Sigma Theory and Out There, amongst others, and are currently hard at work on Out There: Oceans of Time. Let me hand over to Mi Clos' Creative Director and founder, Michael Peiffert to give you loads on insight into the studio and the game... [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1145290/Out_There_Oceans_of_Time/?curator_clanid=35526779]BUT don't forget to wishlist Out There: Oceans of Time on Steam now[/url]. Go on, do it before you forget. Ta. Now, the interview:


[b]When was the studio formed?[/b]

in 2010, I've been laid off from an ad agency after winning a 2M€ contract for them, just after becoming dad for the first time. Thanks to the french unemployment wage, I was in a position where I could decide of my own fate. That's where I decided to realize my kid's dream: making video games. If my ex-employers hadn't laid me off, I could have missed the best opportunity in my life. So thanks to them!


[b]
How did you choose the studio's name?[/b]

Mi-clos means half-opened in French. When I've started learning game development, I've just got sucked up. I couldn't sleep because there was so much stuff to learn and everything was so new and interesting and exciting. That's how I became a game dev zombie.


[b]
How many people work at the studio?[/b]

I've been working with contractors for years that became regular contributors to my projects. I'm glad Modern Wold helps me building a great team to meet the ridiculous ambitions we set for Out There: Oceans of Time. The team for this project will peak at 5 full-time employees and 5 contractors.


[b]How many games has the studio made?[/b]

Space Disorder, Out There, Out There: Omega Edition, Out There Chronicles series, Sigma Theory: Global Cold War


[b]What's your motto?[/b]

If you reach for the stars, you might end up on the moon.


[b]If you had a mascot, what would it be?[/b]

A nebula (not related but I genuinely love Nebula in Guardians of the Galaxy)


[b]What was your inspiration for the name 'Out There: Oceans of Time'?
[/b]
This song that I've been listening in loop while imagining how the game would look and play. The atmosphere and the story are fitting so perfectly I've just borrowed the title (I hope the composer won't get mad at me for that). (editors note: Michael contacted Melodysheep on twitter and he didn't mind at all!)


[b]What was your inspiration for the gameplay?[/b]

OTOT is a natural continuation of the work I've started 5 years ago. It's just the place where I should be and, I hope, where I'll stay for as long as possible. In this game, we took the unforgivable resource management from the classic title mashed up with the character driven story from the Chronicles series - Plus some crazy stuff I can't talk about yet. The main character is Nyx (seen in the teaser trailer), a strong character in Chronicles. Her level of badassery is a major inspiration.


[b]Where is the game set?[/b]

In the continuum space time, of course!


[b]Describe it in your own words[/b]

OTOT is about fighting against the most hostile environment to humankind: space.


[b]If the studio were a radio station, what genre would you play?[/b]

Is there a radio station that plays movie original soundtracks continuously?


[b]Who's the most 'famous' member of the team, and why?[/b]

[url=https://twitter.com/FibreTigre]FibreTigre[/url], our writer, is one of the biggest internet celebrity here in France. Because, you know, internet.

notes.title: New publisher Modern Wolf declare commitment to ethical game development
notes.notes:
New wee indie publisher Modern Wolf announced themselves to the world this week, and made a big show of declaring they are “committed to ethical game development.” Their initial lineup of five games sounds pretty neat, including the next games from the studios behind Neo Scavenger and Out There. More folks in the industry do talk openly about its troubles these days but it’s still rare for a publisher to make a big selling point of how they treat workers, so I asked Modern Wolf CEO Fernando Rizo more about what that means.

“Consumers are starting to care about how their games are made, and we are striving to be the most ethical creator of games around,” he told me.
